headline: Precious Metals and Industrial Commodities Surge on Friday Rally
paragraphs: Precious metals experienced a broad-based Friday rally with silver jumping 9.11 percent, palladium rising 7.21 percent, platinum up 5.72 percent, and gold gaining 3.75 percent to close at $3668.50 per ounce, or EUR 3343.47. This upward momentum helped gold secure its first weekly rise in three weeks, driven by cycle symmetry pointing to a major bottom following recent heavy losses, though sentiment remains fragile as lingering Federal Reserve interest rate hike risks temper the outlook.

Industrial commodities also saw significant gains as copper jumped 5.03 percent to $5.60 per pound, or EUR 5.10, heading for its first weekly gain since early October as short sellers retreated, marking its biggest jump since January. Natural gas rose 6.79 percent to $3.49 per MMBtu, or EUR 3.18, with the breakout holding as momentum builds, despite contrasting reports of prices tumbling on warm US weather forecasts.

In the energy sector, Brent crude fell 3.98 percent to $90.84 per barrel, or EUR 82.79, while WTI crude dipped 0.72 percent, with prices trimming weekly gains ahead of an upcoming OPEC+ meeting and concerns over shipping risks and supply fears. The euro traded at 1.0972 against the US dollar, meaning European buyers faced slightly adjusted import costs for dollar-denominated raw materials.
